mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns due to compression of discount rates in an easing monetary policy environment.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% and employment (PAYEMS) falls below 135,000.0 thousand, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 60% of instances when UNRATE>5.0 and PAYEMS<135000.0, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high consumer spending regime (defined by RSAFS > 350,000.0 million dollars), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns due to strong consumer demand supporting corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when RSAFS>350000.0, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL annual inflation rate rises above 2.0%, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers central bank tightening and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.0%, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (2017=100) and housing starts (HOUST) falls below 2000.0 thousand units, it signals a weakening economy that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 60% of instances when INDPRO<100 and HOUST<2000.0, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is above 2.0% annually, it signals a strong economy that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when GDPC1>2.0%, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.0%), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to increased discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS>4.0 and CPIAUCSL annual change>2.0%, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
